findingsCorrected.finding: The headline heuristic said growing types with stable operations wants polymorphism, and grouped operation-wide updates under When it is not. The later coverage and compatibility sections were more precise. Those broad statements could treat an intentional per-operation review gate as proof that Visitor was the wrong design.
findingsCorrected.consequence: An agent could move unrelated operations into model classes or add a generic fallback solely to avoid useful compile failures, losing evidence that billing, validation or rendering semantics still need a deliberate decision.

findingsCorrected.correction: Qualified the selection rule by operation ownership and required coverage, made the alternatives heading conditional, and explicitly preserved deliberate review of each operation. findingsCorrected.architecturalInference: The compiler/API evidence establishes the mechanisms, not the best design for every system. Valuing per-operation review depends on the project's accepted coverage and ownership contract; that conditional judgment is the correction.

sources.title: Java SE 17 ElementVisitor API
sources.version: Java SE 17; visitModule since 9, visitRecordComponent since 16
sources.supports: An established Visitor can evolve with documented source-compatibility hazards, version-aware abstract helpers and default unknown handling. This is a primary API example of deliberate evolution/fallback contracts.
sources.limits: Does not establish a universal preference for Visitor. Concrete default behavior of a user's implementation still needs inspection.

sources.title: Java Language Specification, Java SE 21, Binary Compatibility
sections: 13.2 What Binary Compatibility Is and Is Not
sources.supports: Source recompilation and binary compatibility are separate; adding interface members and defaults has distinct conditions and conflicts. Sealed evolution does not guarantee old exhaustive consumers have handling for new cases.
sources.limits: Binary compatibility is not semantic new-kind coverage. Exact invocation outcome additionally follows the VM method-resolution rules and was exercised by the isolated fixture.

sources.title: Java Virtual Machine Specification, Java SE 21, invokeinterface
sources.supports: An abstract selected method, or lack of a qualifying concrete implementation under the stated conditions, can yield AbstractMethodError at interface invocation.
sources.limits: Runtime check here used JDK 25 with a Java 21 compilation target, not an installed Java 21 VM.

sources.title: Java SE 21 Pattern Matching for switch
sections: Type Coverage in switch Expressions and Statements
sources.supports: Sealed type coverage and catch-all behavior support the preserved switch alternative; old compiled exhaustive consumers have conditional MatchException risks with evolution.
sources.limits: No local switch version-skew runtime test. One illustrative guide snippet appears inconsistent about which subtype is returned; that snippet was not used as executable proof. The formal coverage conditions/JLS support the preserved qualified claim.

sources.title: Java SE 21 Record Patterns

sources.limits: Unchanged guidance, not evidence for the architectural selection correction.
